AbstractSoils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure.

Tourism is a complex activity involving multiple stakeholders, both public and private. Consequently, the transformation of the sector, in any sense, requires the collaboration of multiple actors and the consideration of its various dimensions, including in regulatory terms. The Goals established in the 2030 Agenda and their embodiment in the concept of sustainable tourism particularly highlight this need.

AbstractClimate change increasingly affects real estate markets because property assets are location-specific and directly exposed to environmental conditions. This study examines whether physical climate risks influence volatility in South African listed property markets. Using a GARCH–MIDAS framework, daily returns from five property indices are linked to monthly indicators of drought, extreme precipitation, and temperature extremes derived from the Actuarial Society of South Africa Climate Index.

abstract: The load capacity factor (LCF) is a preferred sustainability indicator due to its ability to measure the ecological footprint and the biocapacity to support both. However, two drivers of ecological outcomes are gaining popularity, green economic complexity (GEC) and biodiversity finance (BF), but these are both explored in different literatures. The impacts on the climate of their financial policy framework have not been proven.

Abstract Water is essential for life, and effective hydrological management is crucial for economic stability and quality of life. Poor water resource governance can lead to scarcity, displacement, or even fatal consequences. Hydrological conditions in East Africa are influenced by drivers such as demographic expansion, industrialization, droughts, and vegetation dynamics.

AbstractExtreme weather and climate events are increasingly intensified by human-induced global warming, exacerbating risks to ecosystems and society. Yet many global extremes datasets remain coarse and fragmented, limiting local assessments of temperature and precipitation hazards. Here we introduce ERA5-EX, a global 0.1° gridded dataset of single and compound temperature and precipitation extremes from 1950 to 2025 derived from ERA5-Land.

Travel times of long period body waves passing through the lower mantle reveal the deep seismic structure and forces shaping our planet . Manual methods measuring P and S wave arrivals produce travel time catalogs with high internal consistency, but have not kept pace with the rapid growth in waveform records. Here we use attention-based machine learning trained on prior manual datasets to develop a catalog spanning 2010-2023 which is consistent with previous catalogs and straightforward to update.

AbstractTemperature extremes linked to climate change are becoming more frequent and more intense. This has significant implications for human health, including conditions driven by immune dysregulation. There is growing evidence that external thermal stress, particularly heat, may influence both the development and clinical course of several autoimmune conditions.

Climate change represents a profound global crisis and the most significant threat to contemporary agricultural systems. This study evaluates the adoption status of Climate-Smart agricultural (CSA) practices among smallholder households and identifies the key factors influencing their adoption in the West Belesa district of Northwest Ethiopia. This study justifies the gaps in CSA adoption.

Proglacial lakes can accelerate terminus retreat and dynamic thinning of lake-terminating glaciers. However, glacier responses to abrupt lake disconnection following glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) remain poorly quantified. Here, we investigate the dynamic evolution of Jinwu Glacier in southeastern Tibet, China, whose proglacial lake (Jinwuco) drained during a GLOF on 26 June 2020, shifting the glacier from lake- to land-terminating conditions.

Marine heatwaves and coral bleaching pose significant threats to the Great Barrier Reef (GBR), particularly during austral summer when atmospheric conditions can significantly enhance ocean surface warming. One such condition is the development of doldrums, characterised by weak winds and reduced cloud cover, which promote increased solar heating of the ocean surface. When these conditions persist, this buildup of heat can develop into marine heatwaves contributing to widespread coral bleaching.

Neurons represent changes in external and internal environments by altering their activity patterns. While coherent brain-wide patterns of neural activity have been observed in neuronal populations, very little is known about their dimensionality, geometry, and how they are correlated with sensory inputs. Here, we recorded the activity of most head neurons in Caenorhabditis elegans experiencing changes in bacterial or control buffer stimuli around their nose.
